Definition: from G5259 and a derivative of ἐρέσσω (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable):--minister, officer, servant.
BiblicalUsage: The word hypērétēs carries the sense of a servant, a minister, an officer. In Matthew 5:25, the text says "and the judge deliver thee to the officer." In Mark 14:54, the text says "and he sat with the servants."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hypērétēs tells me that serving is not earning; it is answering love with love. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; Jesus Before the Sanhedrin
